title: Towards Lightweight Graph Neural Network Search with Curriculum Graph Sparsification

problem.claim: Graph Neural Architecture Search needs to support resource-constrained scenarios.

gap.claim: Existing Graph Neural Architecture Search studies overlook applications in resource-constrained scenarios.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes GASSIP, a lightweight Graph Neural Architecture Search method combining graph sparsification and network pruning.
GASSIP includes an operation-pruned architecture search module for efficient lightweight GNN search.
GASSIP includes a curriculum graph data sparsification module using architecture-aware edge-removing difficulty measurement to select sub-architectures.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the curriculum graph data sparsification module as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five benchmarks are reported to demonstrate GASSIP's effectiveness.
The method is reported to achieve on-par or higher node classification performance with half or fewer model parameters and a sparser graph.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNAS performs well on graph-structured tasks, but resource-constrained applications are overlooked.
The paper introduces a joint graph-data and architecture mechanism and the GASSIP method for lightweight GNN search.
GASSIP combines operation-pruned architecture search, curriculum graph sparsification, architecture-aware difficulty measurement, and iterative optimization with two differentiable masks.
The authors report effectiveness on five benchmarks and comparable or better node classification performance with substantially fewer parameters and a sparser graph.

source_observation.claim: The method jointly adjusts graph data sparsity and architecture search using architecture-aware edge-removing difficulty.

interpretation.claim: For resource-constrained graph learning, co-designing the input graph and model architecture may reduce computational cost while preserving task performance.

application.claim: Use joint graph sparsification and architecture pruning as a candidate strategy for lightweight graph neural network deployment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish effectiveness beyond the reported five benchmarks or specify the resource constraints and deployment conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five benchmarks, datasets, baselines, or quantitative performance values.
The abstract does not provide computational cost, search time, memory usage, or deployment conditions.
The abstract does not describe the architecture search space, pruning ratios, or optimization details.
